messages:
Support Steph: Hey team, customer reporting a sudden spike of 502s from the hosted API (edge). Started ~12:00 UTC. They can reproduce consistently for certain streaming embedding requests. Sending trace id/truncated logs below.
Customer Alice: Confirmed, our service hit a 15% error rate for ~5m. Request id: req-9a8b7c. Region: prod-us-west2. Happened on both small and medium payloads. Blocking our pipeline.
Support Steph: Repro steps I got from customer: they do a chunked POST to /v1/embeddings with a ~1.2MB JSON payload over keepalive. Curl they used:
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @batch.json
```
Support Steph: Partial edge log snippet for trace req-9a8b7c:
```
[2025-01-12T12:03:14Z] envoy upstream reset before response headers: connection failure
[2025-01-12T12:03:14Z] router: upstream returned 502
[2025-01-12T12:03:15Z] upstream response timed out -> 504
```
Oncall Javi: Thanks — can you paste the exact trace ids and which edge host? we need the full request_id to correlate (not just truncated). Also which customer org?
Support Steph: Full id: req-9a8b7c-2f, org: acme-inc. Edge host: edge-usw2-12. I pulled tail of envoy on that host and saw repeated `connection: close` from upstream auth-proxy.
Eng SRE Mira: Looking at metrics for edge-usw2-12: concurrent upstream connections to billing/auth proxy spiked, connection pool exhausted -> Envoy started returning 502 for new incoming connections. There's also elevated latency on auth check (p99 auth latency ~1.8s). Any config changes around 12:00?
Backend Tom: We pushed a conservative auth-cache TTL change at 12:01 to reduce stale cache hits, which inadvertently increased upstream fanout to auth service (more backend connections). Pool default was 10. Rolling back now to previous config.
Support Steph: Customer says error rate dropped after ~12:10 but a few 502s still trickling. They reported new trace id req-9a8b7c-9 at 12:14 with same pattern.
Eng SRE Mira: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) increase upstream conn pool from 10->40 for auth-proxy, 2) enable per_try_timeout and per-route retry (503->retry) to avoid hard 502s, 3) add short-lived local auth cache warmup to reduce fanout during rotations.
Backend Tom: Deploying change: bumping pool to 40 and adding per_try_timeout=2s on the auth route. Will also add extra structured logs to correlate request_id -> upstream socket. Rolling out now.
Redwood Bot: rollout:service/billing-auth rev487 -> starting deploy to prod-us-west2 (hosts 1/3 -> 3/3).
Oncall Javi: Good. If this recurs, capture tcpdump on edge-usw2-12 for one of the failing request_ids and upload to the private incident bucket. Also flag for a short postmortem if error impact > 5% for more than 10m.
Support Steph: Noted. I told customer the rollback + pool bump are live and asked them to repro and give new trace ids if anything persists. :thumbsup:
Customer Alice: Will test and report back within 20m. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
Support Steph: Closing the immediate escalation. Follow-up: Eng SRE/Mira + Backend Tom to sync and create follow-up runbook item for auth-cache rotations and pool sizing.
